title: Heller et al. (2023) first-cut yield, field harvest and mechanical-pretreatment data
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), per the open-access article/publisher policy; cite the source.
geography: Swabian Alb region and University of Hohenheim research setting, Germany
evidence_class: peer-reviewed primary experimental study; measured analytical/field data and source-fitted kinetic results
applicability: Reference evidence for Phase 1 field-yield/harvest context, Phase 3 mechanical pretreatment, and Phase 5 batch methane yield/kinetics. Does not cover GreenHub Phase 2 storage, Phase 4 protein recovery, Phase 6 upgrading, or Phase 7 nutrient recovery.
measurement_period: The extract records publication year. The specific harvest campaign year/date is not stated in the curated rows; consult article Methods for full campaign context.
handling: Transcribed source-reported values only. No unit conversion, annualization, treatment ranking, curve re-fit, transfer to Dutch supply, or model default activation was performed. Blank cells mean not reported, not applicable, or not treatment-specific as documented by the source table; they are not zero.
major_limitations: Landscape-management material from German orchard/lowland meadow conditions is not GreenHub roadside grass.
Only the first cut is included in the reported site biomass yield; the article notes that a second cut is normally made but is not part of this yield.
AG was used on narrower or tree-covered plots that could not be accessed by the larger tractor/loader wagon, confounding direct equipment comparisons.
Field harvesting energy excludes hand-guided mowing under tree cover, transport to the biogas plant, and downstream handling.
The BMP and modified Gompertz results are batch/research-plant evidence, not continuous-digester performance or a validated process kinetic law for GreenHub.
Table 1 reports TS and VS n=3, acetic acid n=2, and other chemical analyses n=1; it does not print SDs. Do not treat the chemistry as a statistical population estimate.
The article says study data are available from the corresponding authors on reasonable request; replicate-level records are not included in this extract.
source_attribution: Heller, R.; Brandhorst, C.; Hülsemann, B.; Lemmer, A.; Oechsner, H. Energies 2023, 16(24), 8091. https://doi.org/10.3390/en16248091.
source_location: Results §3.1 (yield); Table 2 and Results §3.4 (harvest/pretreatment); abstract and Methods §2.7.1 (incremental energy balance)

column_units_basis.pretreatment_feed_fm_kg_mean: kg fresh matter per reported treatment batch
column_units_basis.reported_incremental_energy_balance_kwh_: source-calculated kWh/t volatile solids; equation compares additional CHP electricity from extra methane against pretreatment specific energy; source assumes 38% electrical CHP efficiency

notes: The field yield is stored once as a study-wide record rather than duplicated across treatment variants.
The reported energy balance is a source calculation, not a direct energy meter and not a cradle-to-gate energy balance. The article's energy calculation assumes 38% electrical CHP efficiency.
